subject: dsa
title: Car Fleet
summary: Sort cars by position, closest to the target first, and walk them keeping each fleet's arrival time on a stack. A car slower than the fleet ahead can't catch up, so it starts a new fleet.
problem: Cars on a one-lane road head to a target and can't pass; count how many fleets arrive.

steps.caption: Cars on a one-lane road can't pass. A slower car ahead bunches faster cars behind it into one fleet. Count the fleets that reach the target.
Arrival time = (target - pos) / speed. Sort by position, closest first, giving these times. Index 0 is the car nearest the target.
The nearest car arrives at time 1 and leads the first fleet.
Next car also arrives at time 1, and 1 <= 1 means it catches the fleet ahead. Same or earlier arrival bunches it in.
Time 7 is later than the fleet ahead (1), so this car never catches up. A later time starts a new fleet.
Time 3 is earlier than the fleet led by 7, so it catches up and merges in.
Time 12 is later than the fleet ahead (7), so this car can't catch up and starts a new fleet.
Three fleet leaders remain, at times 1, 7, and 12. So 3 fleets reach the target.
